The previous tenant left the property around 2008 and failed to close the leasehold title. A copy of the leasehold title is included within the legal pack. Correspondence has been sent to the Insolvency Service to request that the bankruptcy notice and bankruptcy restriction be removed in order to close the leasehold title. The current tenant has been in occupation of the property since 24th August 2016.The Insolvency Service confirmed on 4th July 2019 that they have made an application to HM Land Registry to remove the bankruptcy notices/entries which are preventing the leasehold title of CH521481 (relating to a lease dated 21st May 2004) from being closed. HM Land Registry have been made aware that the Insolvency Service have made a request for the bankruptcy notices/entries to be removed. The Seller's solicitor await a response. In respect of No.75 Witton Street, the tenant E Cig (Cheadle) Limited is being granted a new five year renewal lease from 13th December 2020, subject to contract. The lease will be on the same terms as the existing lease which is included within the legal pack at a rent of £13,000 p.a. It will be a renewal lease with reference to the existing lease. The tenant has agreed to pay the Landlord’s legal fees of £650.00 plus VAT. It is currently in solicitors hands. The tenant has paid the Landlord’s legal fees to the Landlord’s solicitor on Friday 5th July 2019. A draft version of the renewal lease has been sent to the tenant for approval on 8th July 2019. A copy of the draft lease is included within the legal pack. HM Land Registry have now completed the application to close the leasehold title which related to an old lease dated 21st May 2004, where the previous tenant had vacated the premises in 2008 and did not close the leasehold title, for 77 Witton Street and that was noted on the freehold title register for 75 and 77 Witton Street. The renewal lease for 75 Witton Street has been approved, today, by the Tenant’s (The E-Cig Store (Cheadle) Limited) solicitor who confirmed that they will arrange for signature by their client. The renewal lease has also been sent to the seller for execution in readiness for completion.

Freehold Multi-Let Industrial and Ground Rent Investment Opportunity In the Particulars of Sale please note the following changes apply:

In the Tenure paragraph, please note the property which to be sold is held on a Freehold and unmerged Long Leasehold interest. Please refer to the legal pack for further information.

In the Schedule of Accommodation and Tenancies, please note the lease of Unit 3 to A D Victoriam Ltd is for a term of 3 years from 30.01.18 and not as stated. There is a Tenant break option on 30.01.2019 and 30.01.2020.

Footnote (1) please note the rent rises from £10,833.34pa to £13,000pa from 30.01.2019. The Vendor will top up the rent from Completion of the sale until 29.01.2019.

The Tenant of unit 7 The BSS Group have confirmed they are no longer in day-to-day occupation however the lease remains in force and rent is paid up to date.

On the Site plan, the coloured marking is incorrect. Unit 18 should not be shaded green and has not been sold off and Unit 16 as shown on the plan has been sold off on a long leasehold interest. Please refer to the Title documents in the legal pack for clarity.

Please note Completion shall take place 6 Weeks from the Date of Exchange.

On Completion the Buyer shall pay to the Seller the costs of the Searches being £2,043.12 (incl. VAT).

The Arrears Statement in the Legal Pack which shows £22,935.37 outstanding as at 24.01.18 has now been reduced to £19,753.06 as at 01.02.18. An updated statement is available for inspection in the Legal Pack.

auction_events.address_as_published: St Cuthbert's Church, Stockton Road, Hartlepool, County Durham TS25 5AX
auction_events.description: The site is broadly rectangular in shape and extends to approximately 0.74 acres (0.30 hectares). It accommodates St Cuthbert Church, a presbytery, and a parish hall with a commercial kitchen, all of which adjoin one another via a single storey central corridor An undeveloped area of land, previously accommodating a care home which has since been demolished, is located to the south of the site A car park is situated to the east, accessible from Stockton Road. Built in 1928 the presbytery is located to the centre of the site. It is brick built and is covered by a slate hipped roof It has large bay windows to the main gable elevation, decorative quoins and exposed lintels. The dwelling benefits from having two integral garages. Internally, it has a number of reception and office rooms at ground floor level, and five bedrooms with various ancillary rooms at first floor level. Adjoining the presbytery is a large, two storey nave which has a mezzanine floor Internally it has white plastered walls, recessed arched windows to the upper levels and oak panelled doors to the confessionals. A double height parish hall with a suspended ceiling is found to the rear of the site which benefits from having a commercial kitchen. Additional information Tenure Freehold. Accommodation Please note the approximate areas have been provided by the VOA/Vendor/EPC and the property has not been internally inspected by Savills. The photos and yellow line drawings are for illustrative purposes only and may not reflect the exact boundary of the site. The onsite buildings have a total footprint of 13,504 sq ft (1,254.60 sq m) The nave extends to approximately 3,415 sq ft (317 sq m) Tenancy Offered with Vacant Possession. Planning The land is not allocated for any specific land use in the Local Plan and, as such, constitutes ‘white land’. The property falls within the F1 (Learning and non residential institutions) planning Use Class The site is therefore suitable for uses including education, training centres, public libraries, public hall, exhibition halls, law courts or public worship The property is not Grade Listed and is not Locally Listed. The site does not benefit from any form of planning permission at present. Despite this, it is the view of Savills that the property may be suitable for a range of alternative uses, subject to the receipt of planning permission and all other necessary consents.

auction_events.address_as_published: Mullagrach Island Polbain, Achiltibuie, Wester Ross, IV26 2YN
auction_events.description: The Summer Isles are located at the mouth of Loch Broom in the far northwest of Scotland and comprise a group of around 20 islands. Mullagrach Island is the most northerly of the Summer Isles and extends to approximately 88.7 acres. The Isles and skerries are part of the Wester Ross Marine Protected Area and fall within Scotland's first European Geopark. The island itself has a coastline of rocky beaches, sheltered coves, caves, arches and cliffs. To the west the island looks out onto the Minch with the Outer Hebrides as backdrop. The waters are rich in marine life, and seals, dolphins and sometimes minke whales are to be seen. To the south and east, with clear views of the mountains of Skye and Torridon, are the inner waters of the archipelago. These are rich in scallops, prawn (langoustine), lobster and crab as well as mackerel, pollock and sea bass. Lobster and crab can be caught in creels off the landing stage. The wildlife of the island includes great skua, shag, fulmars and greylag geese and otters. The island is rich in biodiversity, having not been grazed by sheep for over 30 years. Before that it was used for summer grazing and there are the ruins of an ancient sheiling on the northeast end of the island. Native plant life is extensive. Shrubby willows, rowan and birch thrive alongside grasses and heathers, ferns and lichen, and a mass of different coastal and moorland wild flowers which include sea pinks, orchids, wild primrose, bluebells, scabious and dog violets. Mullagrach Island, which can easily be reached by boat from the harbours at Ullapool and Old Dornie, and by helicopter, has a landing stage and tackle for a running mooring. There is a high-quality, low environmental impact cabin on the island positioned and designed to withstand the weather conditions, designed and built by Northwoods Design, with a curved, heather clad roof which blends into the landscape. Please see https://www.northwoodsdesign.co.uk/cabins-pods-studios for photographs of the construction process. The interior is well equipped with a kitchen and dining area, wood burning stove and two box beds, while solar panels provide power and there is an outside composting WC. There is a rainwater collection system, but drinking water is bottled. The cabin is sold with its contents, ready for overnight and longer stays. Additional information Tenure Heritable (Scottish Equivalent of English Freehold) Accommodation Approximately 35.9 hectares (88.7 acres) Notes Lindsay McKinley a consultant in the Savills Natural Capital team would be delighted to discuss the attributes of the island with interested parties. Visiting the island can be arranged. Please contact the auctioneer for further information. Please note the areas provided are approximate. auction_events.address_as_published: Mullagrach Island Polbain, Achiltibuie, Wester Ross, IV26 2YN
auction_events.description: The Summer Isles are located at the mouth of Loch Broom in the far northwest of Scotland and comprise a group of around 20 islands. Mullagrach Island is the most northerly of the Summer Isles and extends to approximately 88.7 acres. The Isles and skerries are part of the Wester Ross Marine Protected Area and fall within Scotland's first European Geopark. The island itself has a coastline of rocky beaches, sheltered coves, caves, arches and cliffs. To the west the island looks out onto the Minch with the Outer Hebrides as backdrop. The waters are rich in marine life, and seals, dolphins and sometimes minke whales are to be seen. To the south and east, with clear views of the mountains of Skye and Torridon, are the inner waters of the archipelago. These are rich in scallops, prawn (langoustine), lobster and crab as well as mackerel, pollock and sea bass. Lobster and crab can be caught in creels off the landing stage. The wildlife of the island includes great skua, shag, fulmars and greylag geese and otters. The island is rich in biodiversity, having not been grazed by sheep for over 30 years. Before that it was used for summer grazing and there are the ruins of an ancient sheiling on the northeast end of the island. Native plant life is extensive. Shrubby willows, rowan and birch thrive alongside grasses and heathers, ferns and lichen, and a mass of different coastal and moorland wild flowers which include sea pinks, orchids, wild primrose, bluebells, scabious and dog violets. Mullagrach Island, which can easily be reached by boat from the harbours at Ullapool and Old Dornie, and by helicopter, has a landing stage and tackle for a running mooring. There is a high-quality, low environmental impact cabin on the island positioned and designed to withstand the weather conditions, designed and built by Northwoods Design, with a curved, heather clad roof which blends into the landscape. The interior is well equipped with a kitchen and dining area, wood burning stove and two box beds, while solar panels provide power and there is an outside composting WC. There is a rainwater collection system, but drinking water is bottled. The cabin is sold with its contents, ready for overnight and longer stays. Additional information Tenure Heritable (Scottish Equivalent of English Freehold) Accommodation Approximately 35.9 hectares (88.7 acres) Notes Lindsay McKinley a consultant in the Savills Natural Capital team would be delighted to discuss the attributes of the island with interested parties. Visiting the island can be arranged. Please contact the auctioneer for further information. Please note the areas provided are approximate. auction_events.address_as_published: Former Guisborough General Hospital, Northgate, Guisborough, North Yorkshire TS14 6HZ
auction_events.description: The subject site extends to 1.43 acres (0.58 hectares) and accommodates the former Guisborough Hospital, which is now vacant. The property comprises three sandstone-built buildings which are predominantly two storeys in height, covered by slate hipped roofs. Externally the buildings have decorative masonry quoins on the corner of the elevations and stone lintels supporting the windows, which are a mix of UPVC and timber sash. The stone built-buildings, which are Grade II Listed, are interconnected by a single storey extension, which is believed to have been built in the mid-20 century. To the south of the site there are two red brick buildings which are two storey in height, also covered by hipped slate roofs. These buildings are known as the ‘Ashwood’ building and the ‘Cottage’. Access is currently taken from Church Lane to the north and Northgate to the south west. Additional information Tenure Freehold. Accommodation Please note the approximate areas have been provided by the VOA/Vendor/EPC and the property has not been internally inspected by Savills. The photos and yellow line drawings are for illustrative purposes only and may not reflect the exact boundary of the site. Total gross internal area to measure 35,660 sq ft (3,312 sq m) Tenancy Vacant Possession. Planning The property benefits from detailed planning permission for its Change of Use and Conversion into 34x residential dwellings, which was granted in October 2025 under application reference number R/2025/0229/FFM . The consented scheme will comprise a mix of 17x one beds, 12x two beds and 5x three beds. The total gross internal floor area shall be 35,660 sq. ft. (3,312 sq. m.) whilst the total net sales area shall extend to 26,232 sq. ft. (2,437 sq. m). The average size of the one, two and three bed units will be 585, 866 and 1,180 sq. ft. respectively. Under the approved plans, the main block will become a standalone building, following the demolition of the single storey extension. The main block will be converted into 16x apartments, comprising a mix of 5x one beds, 6x two beds and 5x three beds. The eastern building will also become standalone and will be converted into 8x mews style dwellings, each having their own external entrance, fronting onto the central courtyard. The mix of the mews dwellings will comprise 2x one beds and 6x two beds. The Ashwood building to the south will be converted into 10x one bed apartments, four units of which will benefit from having their own private entrances. A small extension will be added to the northern elevation, accommodating the staircase to serve the remaining first floor apartments. As part of the approved plans, the Cottage to the south will be demolished to make way for parking and areas of open space.

auction_events.address_as_published: Bron Eifion Country House Hotel, Criccieth, LL52 0SA
auction_events.description: The property is a magnificent Grade II listed stone property that was constructed in 1883. It has been crafted from local stone and has a predominately pitched slate roof. The hotel has been maintained to a high standard and has remained under the same ownership and management of the same proprietors for 20 years. The property is detached and arranged over change to basement, ground and two upper floors. It provides an open plan reception area with a lounge, the Llechwedd Room, bar, Garden Restaurant, 17 individually designed bedrooms, staff accommodation and a separate three bedroom bungalow currently used for proprietors accommodation. The current owners have extended the Food & Beverage offering to include the Garden Restaurant. This has created a space perfect for hosting functions and private events, solidifying the hotel’s reputation as one of the North’s foremost wedding venues. HISTORY The hotel is steeped in history with ornate pine panelled walls, stone pillars, and a captivating gallery landing adorned with a beamed vaulted ceiling. It was built in 1883-5 by John E Greaves, millionaire owner of the Llechwedd slate quarries at Blaenau Ffestiniog and developer of Porthmadog as a slate distribution center. The property was designed by himself and his wife, and was first occupied in 1885. It is now a Country House Hotel and has had the same proprietors since 2006. FOOD AND BEVERAGE Bron Eifion provides the Llechwedd Room which has capacity for up to 24 covers and provides casual dining facilities in the day.The Garden Restaurant provides a more formal dining experience with capacity for up to 150 covers. It also offers panoramic garden views. WEDDINGS Bron Eifion is a popular wedding venue and is one of North Wales most beautiful, exclusive use venues. The Llechwedd Room is licensed for weddings for up to 24 guests and The Garden Restaurant is licensed for wedding parties of up to 150 guests. Alternatively, these rooms can be used for christenings, wakes, family gatherings or corporate dinners . EXTERNAL AREAS The site extends to approximately 5 acres and features manicured gardens and woodland. It provides a winding driveway that guides guests from the main road toa gravel car park accommodating approximately 25 vehicles with two EV charging points. There is a Victorian Veranda which runs off the Garden Restaurant that provides outdoor seating for approximately 80 covers. Adjacent, is a stone patio furnished with tables and chairs which provides another separate outdoor seating area. The lawns are well maintained and comprise a pagoda which can be used as a licensed venue for civil ceremonies. The gardens also provide two helipads. VALUE ADD OPPORTUNITIES Planning consent was granted in May 2022 to build three self-contained holiday chalets in the grounds adjacent to the main hotel. The current owners run the hotel as a “lifestyle” business and therefore it only trades5 days a week and is closed for a minimum of 6 weeks in December and January. It is estimated that per year there are 131 days where the hotel is not trading. This creates opportunity to increase revenue and EBITDA. auction_events.address_as_published: Darnet Fort, Darnet Ness, Gillingham, Kent, ME9 7HJ
auction_events.description: A freehold nineteenth-century military sea fort, listed as a scheduled monument that was constructed between 1870-1872 for Naval Sea Defence. Fort Darnet is one of two forts constructed on low islands on opposite sides of the Medway channel. Hoo Island is located just 1Km upstream. They were designed to create a "bottle neck" defence for the river. The pair of forts were built on the recommendation of the Royal Commission on Defence, and were intended to provide an inner line of defence to protect the approaches to the naval dockyard at Chatham. Fort Darnet was originally designed for two tiers of guns mounted in a circle, with a boom strung between them. However, extensive build costs, meant that the boom was never implemented. The fort was built to hold a garrison of 100 men and used for gunnery practice. It was decommissioned for use prior to WW1 but was utilised as an observation post in WW2 with platforms and pillboxes built on top. The fort is still in fair condition, however the magazine level is flooded. The island is only accessible by boat and was used for picnicking and leisure up until the 1980's. It is scheduled under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Areas Act 1979. Additional information Tenure Freehold Accommodation A freehold military sea fort and land (Please refer to the title). Tenancy Vacant.

auction_events.address_as_published: The Oast House, Gas Street, Canterbury, CT1 2PR
auction_events.description: The property is formed of two attached buildings. The original building comprises a mid 19th century Grade II Listed former oast. This is arranged over three storeys and fronts Gas Street. The original building includes a unique feature in the form of a square kiln to the rear which has a pyramid roof. The second building is attached on the western side and is believed to have been built in the 1970s with single storey link to the former oast. This later addition is thought to have originally served as theatre workshops and stores. We understand the property was subject to a change of use to a museum store in the early 1980s and this is believed to be its last use before becoming redundant. Internally, the property is in need of refurbishment / restoration throughout(subject to necessary planning and listed building consents). Externally there is space for surface level parking situated to the north west of the building. The property falls within the Canterbury City Council planning jurisdiction. It is situated within a Conservation Area, Area of Archaeological Importance and the Urban Area Boundary. Additional information Tenure Freehold Planning The property has an outstanding planning application for “Change of use of a former storage facility to provide 07no. residential apartments together with internal and external alterations, the demolition of the existing single storey, flat roof link extension and its replacement with a two-storey link-extension together with the erection of a wall and secure cycle and refuse store.” We understand that the proposed plans include an increase in floor area to 6,889 sq ft. Further details of the planning application can be found under REF: CA/20/02190 on the Canterbury City Council Planning Portal. The decision is still pending consideration, we understand this has been delayed as a result of nutrient neutrality issues.

auction_events.description: A substantial and historic former School which sits within 55 acres of mature grounds and circa 150,738 sq ft of buildings. Kilgraston House and grounds are accessed through an impressive, Category B listed, stone archway, with coach houses on either side, one of which is also Category B listed. There is a long driveway leading to Kilgraston House. Avenues of mature trees line either side of the driveway and it is further flanked by large open fields previously used for grazing. A number of modern extensions have been added to Kilgraston House over the years to create teaching space, dormitory rooms and other facilities associated with the school. A chapel and a theatre space are attached to the main building. The former Stable Block is Category B listed and was most recently used as the junior school. The modern science block was constructed in 2013. There are 106 student bedrooms plus 30 bedrooms for staff housed within the main school buildings. The property also benefits from parking for 6 vehicles. TENANCY DETAILS 33 High Street is let to a private individual T/A The Village Bakehouse, at £6,000 pa for 5 years from 28/03/26. 33a High Street is let to a private individual T/A Moorlands Beauty, at £6,000 pa for 5 years from 01/09/2022. Flat 2 (2 bed) is let to a private individual at £650pcm. 33 and 33a High Street is a three storey property of brick elevations and tiled pitched roof coverings in a prominent position on the High Street. The ground floor is arranged as two individual commercial units with separate entrances and rear exits onto the car park. 33 High Street is The Bakehouse whose lease runs from March 2026 with over 15 years history in this location. 33a High Street is Moorlands Beauty with a lease from October 2022. Both commercial units have single glazed timber window frames and access to the parking at the rear. The upper floors consist of two spacious and well-appointed two bedroom apartments, both of which are self-contained and separately accessed and are let by way of Shorthold Tenancy Agreements. The property has been very well maintained, with independent gas boilers to the apartments. Please note, the cottage at the rear of the building is not included in the sale. LOCATION The property features prominently opposite the junction where Hall Road meets High Street (A522) in the village centre. Upper Tean is easily accessible, being 3 miles off the A50. Cheadle is the nearest town approximately 4 miles to the north. Tean as a village has a convenience store, pharmacy, cafes, pubs, hairdressers, petrol station and a primary school.

Early viewing is strongly recommended. auction_events.description: Attractive Grade II Listed Freehold Vacant Mixed Use Building. Guide Price £800,000+. Total accommodation of 1,566.14 sq m (16,858 sq ft) with a right to use 6 parking spaces in rear car park. The Property, 47 St Giles Street is a principally two storey period Grade II Listed building with mezzanine, attic and extensive basement accommodation, forming part of the established historic townscape. The decorative Bath stone façade is executed in the neoclassical style with rusticated Tuscan columns and sash windows, giving the building strong architectural presence. Originally a 17th century house, the property was acquired by the Freemasons in 1879 and established as a Masonic Hall by 1881. The current structure was designed by Albert Havers and built in 1905–1906, with further remodelling in 1928. Until recently it operated as a Masonic club and events venue.. Freehold. Vacant. A residential scheme has been drawn up which illustrates the potential to create a substantial number of residential units above and/or behind the commercial accommodation, subject to the necessary consents. The property comprises the extensive upper floors of the historic Royal Arcade in the heart of Bournemouth town centre, presenting a rare opportunity to deliver a substantial residential-led refurbishment and conversion project with the planning position already established. The accommodation extends to approximately 2,183 sq m (23,500 sq ft) and benefits from Planning Permission and Listed Building Consent for the creation of a 33-unit residential scheme comprising a mix of one, two and three-bedroom apartments. Significantly, a substantial proportion of the accommodation already benefited from established residential use and consent, with further planning permissions subsequently secured for the additional units required to complete the approved scheme. The majority of the proposed apartments are already physically formed within the existing building configuration, having been historically occupied as residential accommodation. Numerous units retain substantial masonry divisions and existing layouts, with drainage infrastructure remaining at former residential locations, albeit purchasers should rely on their own investigations regarding condition and suitability. The approved scheme provides an attractive mix of accommodation, including numerous duplex apartments together with a number of generously proportioned two and three-bedroom units, several extending to in excess of 100 sq m. In addition, the property includes six office suites extending to approximately 306 sq m (3,294 sq ft), offering future asset management and potential development opportunities, subject to obtaining any necessary consents. Extensive sound testing has already been undertaken and a priced schedule of works has been prepared, providing purchasers with a significant body of due diligence information. auction_events.description: Bedrooms x 20 Bathrooms x 10 The Croft served the local community for many years as a residential care home registered for 22 live-in residents though the owners preferred to work with 20 occupied bedrooms for the sake of improved space and comfort requirements for their residents. The property was developed in three stages with the original house at the front of the site offering accommodation on two floors. Subsequently two extensions were added which significantly increase the footprint of the property as can be viewed in our aerial photography. The Croft has been closed as a care home for some years due to retirement with the current owner continuing to live in the owner's accommodation within the building. It is considered that the property offers scope and potential for a number of future uses, subject to all necessary consents being obtainable. Alternatively, site redevelopment may be a further option that prospective purchases may wish to consider, subject to all the necessary consents being obtainable. Accommodation 22 bedrooms, many with en-suite facilities, three communal lounges, kitchen, laundry room, dining room and office/conservatory, three further bath/shower rooms. Outside Substantial car parking area to the front and side, space for numerous vehicles in a courtyard garden side garden in need of cultivation. Auctioneer's Note In addition to the outside space detailed above, as can be viewed from the identification plan in the sales particulars, there is a long strip of land running to the southeast of The Croft. The current owner has had previously entered into negotiations with three neighbouring home owners with a view to transferring this land in sections to these home owners in return for a fee of £10,000 per parcel with the purchaser also meeting legal fees. This information is passed on as described to us by the current owner and prospective purchasers should of course rely on their own enquiries. Local Planning Authority Isle of Wight Council. Website: iow.gov.uk. Tel: 01983 823552. EPC Rating C (54). Total Floor Area 551 sq.m. Freehold with Vacant Possession The Croft, Hooke Hill, Freshwater, Isle Of Wight

auction_events.description: For sale via auction - fees, terms and conditions apply. This substantial property displays some the finest architectural features the Victorian period has to offer & in abundance! Occupying a prominent location on the sought after, Park Avenue & sat handsomely within a large front garden, behind wrought iron railings. The grand entrance archway, double vestibule doors & towering gables project one of the most notable facades on the Avenue. Stepping into the front porch you are greeted with the elegance & grandeur of the large entrance door, retaining the original stained glass with intricate patterns & craftmanship. Victorian wall tiling brings colour & period warmth to this porch, together making the greatest of first impressions to your visiting guests & a warming welcome home! As you enter the grand hallway you are met with pitch pine architrave, towering skirting & Lincrusta panelling. Large, ornate plasterwork adorns the ceiling, framed by a fabulous Lincrusta frieze & magnificent corbels support a vast central archway. The sitting room, presents 12" timber skirting, fabulous stepped plaster cornicing & an impressively detailed plasterwork rose to the ceiling. Natural daylight floods the room through a huge bay window, while your gaze is drawn to the elegant feature fire surround & cast iron fireplace within. The modern & calming colour palette makes this room bright & welcoming, the overwhelming feeling is of period grandeur in this room & throughout the rest of this property. Double, glazed doors lead through into the drawing room which is currently configured as a kitchen diner. You are again presented with an abundance of Victorian features on a grand scale including huge stepped cornicing, a grand ceiling rose, 12" timber skirting & a Victorian fitted cupboard with panelled doors. A further large walk-in bay window floods this beautiful reception room in natural daylight & offers views across the rear garden. The dining room is across the central hallway & up to the front of the property, this imposing & grand reception room boasts the West gables' huge bay window. Dramatic plaster cornicing adorns the ceiling, a magnificent plasterwork ceiling rose is the centre piece & focal point of this room while pitch pine sash windows, picture rails & gigantic skirting frame the room with period splendour. This room is currently configured as the principal suite of the hotel, with a large ensuite bathroom & vast proportions! Back out to the grand hallway & through to the rear of the property, you pass the craftmanship of the central staircase & a arrive at glazed door, leading out to the rear terrace patio & substantial grounds beyond. Off & to the left are the staff quarters, consisting of a rear lobby, a spacious staff or accessible W.C, the main kitchen, laundry corridor & laundry room. Beyond are the house managers accommodation, a spacious studio apartment with views across the rear garden. The wide, central, sweeping staircase is flanked by a decorative newel post, intricately carved from a solid piece of rich, polished Oak. The handrail of the same timber is atop a forest of carved spindles, leading up to a magnificent gallery landing. There is an exquisite 6-panel stained glass window on the mid landing which floods the whole area in vibrant colour with natural daylight, this Palatial reception hallway is drenched in period elegance. The vast central landing is a continuation of the grandeur of the reception hallway below, leading you to 6 generous bedrooms, four with ensuite bathrooms & a large office which sits above the front entrance door. Sweep around the galleried balustrade & through a further archway & you arrive at an internal lobby, a flight of stairs leads up to the 2nd floor accommodation & doors lead to a guest W.C & a further landing beyond which provides access to two further shower rooms & another guest W.C. Up to the second floor & you arrive at the bedroom corridor where you presented with a further five, spacious, double bedrooms, all with ensuite bathrooms. Out & to the rear of the property is bright & spacious courtyard garden, sandstone steps lead down from the house to a terraced patio of crazy paving & from here is a lawned area, finishing at a raised border with mature planting. The grounds open up to further more substantial lawn which encircle a magnificent weeping Willow beyond which is the secure walled car park. This paved area is accessed by double gates from the rear & would comfortably provide parking for six to eight vehicles following a programme of upgrading. This sale of thi

Bowlish House is far more than a conventional hotel. It is a property shaped by nearly three centuries of history, adaptation and reinvention — a private house that evolved into a country hotel, a respected restaurant with rooms, a wedding and celebration venue, an exclusive-use retreat and an atmospheric location for photography and filming. Now offered for sale by auction, it represents a rare opportunity for a new owner to continue that story. The Property The approach to Bowlish House immediately establishes its presence. Its classical Palladian frontage, traditional sash windows, stone detailing and architectural symmetry create a striking first impression, while original and historic features found throughout the building reinforce its Grade II* status. The main house provides eight individually styled guest bedrooms together with an impressive range of communal accommodation. The reception spaces are one of the property’s greatest strengths. Generously proportioned lounges and dining rooms provide welcoming areas for hotel guests, private dining, afternoon teas and intimate celebrations. The ballroom creates a memorable setting for weddings, events, music, dining and larger gatherings, while the orangery provides a light-filled connection between the house and gardens. Throughout the property, period character is combined with the practical accommodation required for hospitality use. Decorative panelling, the traditional staircase, fireplaces, high ceilings and individual room layouts give Bowlish House an identity that would be difficult to reproduce within a modern hotel building. Eight Guest Bedrooms The hotel accommodation comprises eight individually presented bedrooms, offering guests a distinctive alternative to standardised chain-hotel accommodation. The rooms vary in size, design and character, making them suitable for leisure stays, wedding guests, exclusive-use bookings and private group accommodation. Their individuality forms an important part of the Bowlish House experience and provides an excellent foundation for a boutique hospitality operator wishing to develop a strong and memorable brand. Prospective purchasers should to the floorplans and legal documentation for the precise room arrangement, bathroom provision and accommodation schedule. Weddings, Events and Exclusive Use Bowlish House offers considerable potential as an intimate wedding and events destination. Its combination of reception rooms, ballroom, orangery, guest bedrooms and garden areas allows celebrations to take place under one roof, with accommodation available for principal guests. The house is particularly well suited to buyers seeking an alternative to larger and more corporate wedding venues. Alongside weddings, the property could accommodate private dining, milestone celebrations, corporate retreats, creative workshops, Christmas and New Year gatherings, wellness stays and exclusive-use weekends. The opportunity is not simply to sell rooms, but to sell the experience of having an historic Somerset house available for a private occasion. Hotel and Hospitality Opportunity Bowlish House has an established history as a hotel and restaurant with rooms. For an experienced hotelier, chef, events operator or hospitality entrepreneur, the property provides the chance to relaunch and reposition an existing destination without having to create the character of the building from the ground up. Its future could include a boutique hotel, restaurant with rooms, wedding venue, exclusive-use retreat, private members’ destination or a combination of complementary uses. auction_events.description: For Sale Via Online Auction. Fees Apply. We are delighted to offer for sale this attractive parcel of pasture land extending to approximately 5.23 acres, occupying a highly accessible position on the southern outskirts of Rugby with direct road frontage onto Barby Lane. This versatile parcel of land offers an excellent opportunity for those seeking agricultural or equestrian use, benefiting from a level layout and being divided into three well-fenced paddocks, enclosed by mature hedgerows and established trees which provide both privacy and shelter. The land enjoys direct vehicular access from Barby Lane via a secure steel-gated entrance. Positioned adjacent to the entrance is a useful timber-framed agricultural building with breeze block construction, tiled flooring and a clear PVC sheet roof, together with a small extension. Towards the rear of the land is a further timber pole lean-to, providing additional storage or shelter. Extending to approximately 5.23 acres, the land is classified as Grade 3 agricultural land and consists predominantly of base-rich loam and clay soils. The pasture is relatively level and still displays areas of historic ridge and furrow, adding to its rural character. A natural watercourse runs through the land, providing a convenient natural water supply and drinking point for livestock, making the holding particularly well suited for grazing. Ideally situated between the popular suburb of Hillmorton and the sought-after village of Barby, the land enjoys a peaceful rural setting whilst remaining conveniently located approximately three miles from Rugby town centre and around four miles from Junction 18 of the M1 motorway, offering excellent links to the M1, M6, A5 and A14. The property is offered for sale freehold with vacant possession. Prospective purchasers should note that the sale will be subject to a 30-year overage clause, reserving 30% of any uplift in value resulting from future non-agricultural or non-equestrian development. The overage will be triggered upon either the implementation of planning permission or any future sale. The property is also subject to a restrictive covenant preventing the erection or placement of any dwelling, caravan, house on wheels, temporary building or encampment intended for residential occupation. A public footpath crosses the centre of the land, and purchasers should satisfy themselves as to its position. The land is enclosed by fencing, and whilst every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy of the plan and description, these are provided for identification purposes only. Constructed principally of local rendered stone beneath a pitched slate roof, the building displays the restrained proportions and simple elegance characteristic of the Georgian period, with later Victorian alterations reflecting its long- established use as a public house. More recently, a single storey 1970's flat roof extension has been added with a cellar below. There is also a garage and large customer car park. the building measures approximately 291 sq m (3,130 sq ft). Situated on the upper floors is well-proportioned private owner's accommodation, providing on-site living ideally suited to owner- occupation or management use. Some refurbishment is required to update and refresh the property. SITUATION The Kings Head occupies a highly visible position on St Andrews Road (A3066), one of the principal routes into the historic market town of Bridport. Situated at the edge of the established residential community of Bradpole, the property benefits from excellent roadside prominence, consistent passing traffic and a loyal local catchment, whilst remaining within easy reach of Bridport town centre. The surrounding area comprises a well-established mix of residential neighbourhoods, schools, local businesses and employment areas, creating year-round trade potential from both local residents and passing visitors. Bridport is one of Dorset's most vibrant market towns, renowned for its independent retailers, twice-weekly street market, thriving arts and food scene, and year-round calendar of festivals and events. Site boundaries are predominantly defined by metal or timber palisade fencing and brick walls, although certain areas comprise dense hedgerows, overgrown vegetation, or open boundaries. auction_events.address_as_published: Horsforth Cemetery Chapel, Calverley Lane, Horsforth, Leeds, West Yorkshire LS18 4DZ
auction_events.description: A former Victorian cemetery chapel situated within the grounds of Horsforth Cemetery and offering potential for restoration and alternative use. Dating from 1881, the stone-built property is of Gothic Revival design and features a central square tower topped by a tall slated spire. Other architectural details include pitched slate roofs, pointed-arched openings, stone buttresses, carved crosses and a traceried window. Internally, the accommodation includes the principal former chapel and worship space, together with additional rooms arranged over the ground and first floors. The building retains stained-glass windows and a number of period features. The property represents an unique opportunity for a purchaser seeking a character building with potential for a range of alternative uses, subject to obtaining the necessary consents. Prospective purchasers should satisfy themselves regarding the building’s condition, services, internal configuration and suitability for their intended use. The property is situated within the established grounds of Horsforth Cemetery, approximately five miles north-west of Leeds city centre. The cemetery can be accessed from Calverley Lane and Victoria Mount, with the chapel approached via the internal cemetery roads. Horsforth is a popular and well-established suburb offering a range of shops, cafés, restaurants and other amenities, principally around Town Street and New Road Side. The area benefits from good road and public transport connections, including rail services from Horsforth station and access to Leeds city centre, Bradford and Leeds Bradford Airport.

auction_events.address_as_published: Colebrook Manor, Former Care Home, Plymouth, Devon PL7 4DZ
auction_events.description: A substantial and versatile former care home offering considerable development potential. Suitable for a variety of alternative uses, subject to any necessary planning consents. Could be reinstated as a care home – all core infrastructure and fixtures remain in situ. Occupying a commanding position set back from Boringdon Road in the established residential suburb of Plympton, the property provides an exceptional opportunity for developers, investors and operators. The property is understood to have originated as a pair of semi-detached Victorian dwellings, with evidence of their existence on local mapping from 1884–1905. The two dwellings were subsequently combined and extensively altered and extended during the 1990s, when the property was converted into a residential care home. A further addition to the north-west corner was completed circa 1996. The building is not listed and falls outside the Plympton St Maurice Conservation Area. The property is subject to a 999 year lease expiring 11/06/3005 The property is offered with what is widely regarded as a virtual freehold interest, held by way of a 999-year leasehold title (DN537743) expiring 11 June 3005, with the freehold vested in DGM London Road Limited (DN371941). The lease appears to be exceptionally permissive in nature. Based on a review of its terms, there is no restriction on use other than in accordance with the title to the property, and the freeholder does not appear to require consent for alterations, structural works, redevelopment or change of use. The lease also appears to be silent on demolition, suggesting no leasehold restriction in that regard, subject always to the necessary statutory and planning consents. Assignment, subletting and mortgage are unrestricted, with only a modest administrative notice and registration requirement. The freeholder's covenants include quiet enjoyment, providing the leaseholder with a strong assurance of undisturbed occupation throughout the term. Prospective purchasers are strongly advised to instruct a suitably qualified solicitor to review the lease in full and satisfy themselves as to the extent, nature and any limitations of the leasehold title prior to exchange of contracts.

The main property also has a gated driveway to the rear with access to a double detached garage. The proposed semi-detached properties will each comprise an entrance hallway, guest cloakroom wc, dining kitchen to the front elevation, and a rear lounge with bi-fold doors opening onto the garden. To the side will be a tandem driveway, while the first floor will provide three bedrooms and a family bathroom. Further details can be found on the local authority planning portal under application reference 24/01435/OUT We believe the proposed dwellings will prove highly desirable, occupying a popular and convenient residential position in the heart of Littleover village centre. The Location - The property occupies a convenient location just a short stroll from Littleover Village centre to include an excellent range of local shops and amenities. This location is also well positioned for employment opportunities at Rolls-Royce, Toyota, Derby University and The Royal Derby Hospital. auction_events.description: A rare opportunity to acquire a substantial freehold former country inn occupying an outstanding rural position within the Pennines, comprising a historic public house, extensive owner's accommodation, a separate four-bedroom house and a self-contained two-bedroom apartment. Dating back to 1610, the property sits within approximately 0.55 acres and enjoys panoramic views across open moorland, offering significant potential for a variety of redevelopment opportunities, such as a high-end residential scheme, subject to any necessary consents. The public house has traded successfully for centuries as a destination venue, particularly for food-led trade, benefiting from its position on the Pennine Way and close to Widdop Reservoir. Although the business ceased trading following the departure of the previous tenant in March 2025, the property retains a premises licence and presents an opportunity for a new operator to re-establish the business or explore alternative uses, subject to obtaining any required consents. The accommodation comprises a traditional bar arranged over two sections with catering kitchen and ancillary areas, together with generous three-bedroom owner's accommodation. Adjoining the pub is a deceptively spacious four-bedroom house with multiple reception rooms, whilst a separate self-contained two-bedroom apartment occupies the first and second floors above the integral garage/store. Externally, the property benefits from customer seating areas, gardens and a substantial car park serving the premises. Occupying an idyllic countryside setting approximately five miles from Hebden Bridge and eight miles from Colne, the property lies within an area renowned for walking, cycling and outdoor pursuits, attracting visitors throughout the year. Its unique character, sizeable accommodation and picturesque location combine to create an exceptional lifestyle and investment opportunity.

auction_events.description: This delightful period stone house stands in an enviable position adjacent to and backing onto open pasture forming part of the Althorp Estate in one of the most sought after locations in Northamptonshire. The house is believed to date from the early 19th Century constructed of ironstone beneath a part thatch and part slate roof and offers considerable scope for modernisation and refurbishment to the three bedroomed accommodation with potential for extension into the attached outbuilding subject to planning permission. Formally the village Post Office and now vacant the property retains a wealth of character features and stands in private gardens extending to just under a quarter of an acre. Tenure Freehold The property stands in the Harlestone village Conservation Area and is NOT a Listed building. The house forms part of the Althorp Estate and will be sold subject the Estate standard schedule of covenants. ACCOMMODATION GROUND FLOOR Reception hall, living room, Post Office servery, store, cloakroom, dining room, kitchen, pantry and porch. FIRST FLOOR Landing, bedroom one, bedroom two, bedroom three, bath/shower room. OUTSIDE The house stands back from the road behind the deep front garden bounded by paled fencing and a pathway leads to the front door flanked either side by lawns and well stocked flower and shrub borders containing a variety of mature small trees including Holly, Laurel, Oak, Sumac and Magnolia. The garden continues on the eastern side of the house where there is a former kitchen garden once used for the production of vegetables and bounded by post and rail fencing. A doorway leads to the courtyard. OUTBUILDINGS Workshop, fuel store, wood store and external WC. REAR GARDEN Laid to lawn housing the now derelict greenhouse and the oil storage tank, the rear garden is bounded by post and rail fencing and Beech hedging and contains a number of mature shrubs and small trees backing directly onto open pasture. HISTORICAL NOTE AND PLANNING The property stands in the Harlestone village Conservation Area and is NOT a Listed building. The house forms part of the Althorp Estate and will be sold subject the Estate standard schedule of covenants. AGENTS NOTE THE GARDEN STANDING TO THE EASTERN SIDE OF THE HOUSE WAS ONCE USED FOR THE PRODUCTION OF VEGETABLES AND IS BOUNDED BY POST AND RAIL FENCING. THIS AREA IS EXCLUDED FROM THE SALE BY AUCTION HOWEVER, IT WILL BE OFFERED TO THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER BY SEPARATE CONTRACT AT A PRICE OF £35,000 IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THE COMPLETION OF THE SALE. SHOULD THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER FAIL TO TAKE UP THE OPTION TO PURCHASE WITHIN FOUR WEEKS, THIS LAND WILL BE RETAINED BY THE ALTHORP ESTATE, AND THE BUYER WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ERECTING NEW BOUNDARY FENCES AND WALLS ALONG THE PARTY BOUNDARY. Energy Efficiency Rating (EPC) Current Rating E Services Interested parties are requested to make their own enquiries to the relevant authorities as to the availability of services. auction_events.address_as_published: Kirkfield End, Colvend, Dalbeattie DG5 4QE
auction_events.description: Looking for a versatile investment opportunity, or somewhere to escape? This property lends itself to being an ideal holiday let, AirBnB, or second home. Based on local property values, this has been heavily discounted, to facilitate a quick sale. Set on the outskirts of the coastal village of Rockcliffe, and accessed via a long shared driveway, the property is in a beautiful spot with spectacular views. Accommodation comprises a hallway, lounge/diner, kitchen, the second bedroom and house bathroom. The main bedroom can be found on the upper floor and is a good sized double, with storage. Externally there is garden to the side, front and rear which gives view to Rockcliffe Bay and Rough Island. Please note: that there are external photos showing detail of property which does not form part of this listing. Location - Rockcliffe is a beautiful coastal village, popular with locals and tourists alike for both its' sandy beach and local coastal walks to Castle Point and Sandyhills beach in one direction, and Kippford with its' marina, 2 pubs and a tea room. Dalbeattie is nearby, with a variety of shops, supermarkets, cafes, pubs, restaurants and hotels including the Granite Kitchen, Birchtree and Kings Arms Hotels and many more. There is also a large modern Health Centre, pharmacy, garden centre with coffee shop, library, cinema, Post Office and Town Hall available for community use. The surrounding area offers a wide range of country pursuits including sailing, horse riding, mountain and e-biking (famous Mountain Bike Trail in Dalbeattie Forest), fishing, bird watching, shooting and numerous coastal and woodland walks. The Solway Coast’s popular seaside villages with sandy beaches are close by at Rockcliffe, Sandyhills and Southerness. Rockcliffe is an ideal base for exploring the Colvend Coast and the region's castles and gardens.

Maps & Location Map Street View Satellite Falkirk sits in Scotlands Central Belt on the south side of the upper Firth of Forth, roughly 20 miles north-east of Glasgow and 23 miles west of Edinburgh. The town itself has a population of around 35,500 and forms the commercial and administrative heart of a tightly clustered urban area that also includes Grangemouth, Larbert, Stenhousemuir, Camelon and Polmont. That wider built-up area exceeds 100,000 people, while the Falkirk Council area as a whole is home to about 160,000. The town is a well-established commuter and retail catchment for both Glasgow and Edinburgh, served by the M9 and M876 motorways and by two principal stations: Falkirk High on the main GlasgowEdinburgh line (typically 2028 minutes to Glasgow Queen Street and 2435 minutes to Edinburgh Waverley) and the more central Falkirk Grahamston on the EdinburghDunblane route. Additional stations at Larbert, Polmont and Camelon, frequent bus services to the two cities and Stirling, and proximity to Edinburgh Airport (c. 20 miles) and Glasgow Airport (c. 33 miles) give the town strong strategic connectivity across the Central Belt. auction_events.description: A substantial and unusual freehold investment/development opportunity comprising a two-bedroom terraced house, a large adjoining vacant site formerly occupied by a public house, together with a separate jitty/access – all included within one freehold title. Offered for sale by auction is this exciting opportunity at 34 & 36 Second Street, presenting considerable scope for investors, developers and builders looking for a project with significant potential. The lot comprises an existing two-bedroom terraced house, a substantial vacant plot where a former public house previously stood, together with a separate jitty/access area. The whole is being sold together under one freehold title. The existing house extends to approximately 64 sq. metres according to the floorplan and is arranged over two floors. The accommodation comprises a living room and kitchen/dining area to the lower floor, with two bedrooms and a bathroom above. The property is currently in a poor condition and requires a comprehensive programme of refurbishment and repair, making it ideally suited to an experienced investor, builder or developer. Once renovated, the house offers the opportunity to create a two-bedroom residential property alongside the wider potential offered by the adjoining land. Of particular interest is the large vacant site adjoining the house, formerly occupied by a public house. The site provides a substantial area of predominantly cleared land and could offer considerable scope for redevelopment, additional residential accommodation or alternative uses, subject to all necessary planning permissions and consents. Also included within the freehold is a separate jitty/access running between the surrounding properties, connecting through towards the main road. The combination of an existing dwelling, sizeable former pub site and additional access makes this a particularly interesting proposition with numerous potential asset-management and redevelopment possibilities. The property is situated within an established residential area, with local amenities and transport connections readily accessible. The wider area also benefits from proximity to the Durham Heritage Coast. Key Features Substantial freehold development/investment opportunity 34 & 36 Second Street offered as one lot Existing two-bedroom terraced house House extends to approximately 64 sq. metres Requires extensive refurbishment and repair Large adjoining vacant plot Site formerly occupied by a public house Separate jitty/access included within the freehold Potential for redevelopment or additional accommodation, subject to planning Excellent opportunity for builders, developers and investors Vacant possession of the house and main former pub site Tenure: Freehold Please note: Given the condition of the existing building, prospective purchasers should make their own enquiries regarding its structural condition and suitability for refurbishment. Post 47. Title number is ABN97934. Located on a low mound on the south side of a field boundary 150 yards east of an un-named minor road. Daily local bus service connecting with Aberdeen (26 miles). The Bunker was not required to fulfil its nuclear war role. With international relations having changed radically, the British government cancelled plans for upgrading and is sold on a freehold basis. Opened in 1962 and closed 1991. Secured with padlock entry. Freehold Sale. Full outright ownership. PRIME LOT IN EXCLUISVE AREA - VERY RARE TO MARKET - PRICED TO SELL. Alford is a large village in Aberdeenshire, north-east Scotland, lying just south of the River Don. It lies within the Howe of Alford which occupies the middle reaches of the River Don. United Kingdom Warning and Monitoring Organisation (UKWMO) Royal Observer Corps Post (ROC) Post. The bunker was designed to accommodate three people for two weeks. It has an underground monitoring room and a chemical toilet. All surface features remain intact with some flaking of the khaki paint. The unit is padlocked and secured. Title Number: ABN97934. Internally the post is very neat and tidy with many items remaining including WB1401 carrier receiver with WB1410 filter unit, Tele-talk, tool board, small wall mounted shelf, mirror, visitors log, various papers, ROC magazines, fire blanket in its box, dustpan, original canvas folding chair, FSM probe gasket, candle holder, light/wiring, BT junction boxes/wiring, BPI mount, posters, kettle, saucepan, washing bowl, cleaning materials, fuse box/wiring, net, pick axe, newspaper cutting about the post. On the wall the crew have written Stand Down - Best Post 29 Group. There is a wooden sign that says 47 Post Alford. Some items from the post have been donated to the Alford Heritage Centre where they have an ROC Room with artifacts from other local posts and Aberdeen Group HQ. The property comprises extensive industrial accommodation including a detached office building, two inspection sheds, a machine shop with integrated two-storey offices, a detached workshop and office building, terraced workshops, swarf shed, extensive concrete and hardcore surfaced yards, pipe storage areas and areas of undeveloped land. The site has been developed to support large-scale industrial and engineering operations, benefitting from substantial external storage and yard areas, extensive parking provision and two 10-tonne overhead gantry cranes within the principal machine shop. The detached office accommodation provides a range of open plan and partitioned offices, meeting space, welfare facilities and passenger lift access. The site occupies a prominent position immediately adjacent to the A90 dual carriageway, one of the principal arterial routes connecting Aberdeen and Dundee, providing road access to the wider North East of Scotland and beyond. Vehicular access is taken via the B966, which adjoins the A90 approximately 1 mile to the north east of the property. The surrounding area is characterised by a mixture of industrial, rural and agricultural land uses. The property's strategic location provides connectivity to Aberdeen, Scotland's principal energy and port-related hub, whilst Laurencekirk offers access to local amenities and services. Aberdeen Harbour, including its South Harbour expansion, lies to the north and provides deep-water port facilities serving domestic and international shipping routes, whilst Aberdeen International Airport offers both passenger and freight services. auction_events.address_as_published: Frankwell, SHREWSBURY , Shropshire, SY3 8JY
auction_events.description: Location! Location! Location! Situated on the highly desirable central west side of Shrewsbury's historic town centre, this property is just a stone's throw from the town centre in Frankwell. Walk across the Welsh Bridge to Shrewsbury's vibrant town centre, offering an abundance of boutique shops and quirky independent stores tucked away in medieval alleyways. The town also boasts a fantastic array of cafes, restaurants, and wine bars, many of which sit right on the riverside. Don't forget the famous Quarry Park, which hosts superb events throughout the year. Within walking distance of some of Shrewsbury's most well-respected schools, sites, and attractions, living in Frankwell is a lifestyle choice. It sits in the heart of Shrewsbury, yet is just far enough away, surrounded by historic buildings that form the character and history we all love in Shrewsbury. Take a short walk and you can be sitting on the decking of The Boathouse next to the River Severn, enjoying a drink and some fantastic food. Being within walking distance of the train and bus stations is a real bonus; now add easy access to Shrewsbury's major roads heading west and south without even crossing the town centre. A little bit about the property This property is not just super-sized; it has so many options. Currently, the ground floor is used as a large retail shop with a separate stock room and a downstairs room that can be used as an office. The first floor is a very large two-bedroom apartment with a spacious kitchen-lounge-diner and a lovely bathroom, and bedroom two has its own WC. From the first floor, a separate stairwell leads to additional accommodation: a very useful studio apartment with its own en-suite shower room. It is worth noting that each floor has its own access. From an Investment Point of View This property has all the potential to generate a good return. We believe the shop portion could be rented out for around £2,000 per month, and the vendors already have an interested party. On a Site of Approximately 0.04 Hectares (0.118 Acres) Description The property comprises a 16 century detached three storey Grade II listed former public house, retaining a wealth of character and period features throughout. Internally, the ground floor provides the principal trading areas, comprising two bar areas, a restaurant/dining room, breakfast room, commercial kitchen and office accommodation, together with a basement cellar. The upper floors provide owners' accommodation comprising 2/3 bedrooms, in addition to six en-suite guest letting bedrooms, extending to approximately 732 sq m (7,879 sq ft) GIA. Externally, the property benefits from a small courtyard to the rear, accessed via Weybridge Street. The total site extends to approximately 0.04 hectares (0.118 acres). Location The Queen's Head Hotel is prominently situated on St James Street in the historic market town of Monmouth, occupying a prominent corner position within the town centre. Monmouth is located at the confluence of the Rivers Monnow and Wye, approximately 2 miles from the England and Wales border, and serves as a popular gateway to the Wye Valley and surrounding countryside. Monmouth is a well established tourist destination, renowned for its rich history, attractive town centre and range of independent retailers, cafés, restaurants and visitor attractions. The town is home to Monmouth Castle, the birthplace of King Henry V, and the historic Monnow Bridge, one of the few remaining fortified medieval bridges in Britain. The property is situated less than 100 metres from the River Wye and is well placed to capitalise on tourism associated with the Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and the nearby Forest of Dean. The location provides convenient access to a range of regional attractions and outdoor pursuits, including walking, cycling, canoeing and heritage tourism. Monmouth benefits from good road connectivity via the A40, providing links to the M4 and wider motorway network. The town is situated approximately 16 miles north of Chepstow, 18 miles south of Hereford, 26 miles west of Gloucester and 36 miles north east of Cardiff. auction_events.description: Commercial Development Auction House Birmingham are proud to present this former brass foundry and ironmongers, offering investors and developers the opportunity to explore a new future for a distinctive piece of Wolverhampton’s industrial heritage. Historically associated with William Evans, Son & Co., the site’s manufacturing roots extend back to around 1854, with the present building believed to date from around 1870. The company’s activities included brass founding and lock manufacturing, followed by its longstanding role as an ironmongers and builders’ merchant. Council heritage records describe the property as a rare surviving example of a nineteenth-century industrial complex within the City, a compelling story for an investor seeking a project with its own identity. The property requires complete improvement and refurbishment throughout, presenting a substantial project for purchasers experienced in restoring and adapting older buildings. Its history could become a central feature of a sympathetic refurbishment, giving future accommodation a distinctive connection to Wolverhampton’s manufacturing past. Investors may wish to investigate options such as refurbished commercial premises, studios or workspace, or whether residential accommodation or a mixed-use arrangement could be achievable. These are illustrative ideas only, subject to the building’s suitability, structural assessment, financial viability and all necessary planning permissions, building regulations approvals and other relevant consents. No feasibility assessment or approval for these suggestions is implied. We are advised that the front of the building lies within a conservation area, while published council records also identify the property as locally listed. Its heritage therefore offers both a marketing identity and an important consideration for any proposed works. Purchasers should establish the extent of the designations and applicable requirements directly with the local authority. Please contact us at Auction House Birmingham for any enquiries. auction_events.description: Auction House Scotland is delighted to bring to market this substantial brownfield site approximately 15.8 acres in West Fife The site now comes to auction with an attractive guide price of £800,000. Castlehill sits directly off the A907 between Dunfermline and Alloa, close to key transport links including the Kincardine Bridge. Formerly associated with mining operations, the site’s former industrial buildings have since been demolished. What remains are concrete hardstandings, an internal roadway and an existing formed entrance with approved visibility splays. Tree-lined boundaries screen the site, with woodland to the south and east. The site has a planning history that gives it a strong development precedent. Planning permission in principle for 38 houses and 6 live/work units was granted on part of the site in 2015 (Ref. 15/00816/PPP) and has since lapsed. More recently, Fife Council granted full planning permission in July 2025 for a change of use to a holiday lodge park, subject to conditions (Ref. 24/00111/FULL). The approved layout shows 92 lodges, although alternative layouts and unit numbers may be possible, subject to any necessary approvals. The consent also includes a Class 1 retail unit and a path link to the adjacent West Fife Cycleway. The principal pre-commencement condition, relating to contaminated land, has already been discharged. The permission must be implemented by 1 July 2028 and is accompanied by a Section 75 Agreement. Buyers may also wish to investigate alternative proposals such as storage, trade units, commercial workspace, renewable energy or a mix of residential and commercial uses. These alternatives do not currently benefit from the permissions described above and would require separate assessment and any necessary consents. An existing water supply and electricity connection are reported on site. Purchasers should verify their condition, availability and capacity for any proposed use. Planning, title and available technical documentation will be provided in the legal pack. Prospective purchasers must review the legal pack and carry out their own due diligence before bidding. They should satisfy themselves regarding planning conditions, the Section 75 Agreement, access rights, ground conditions, former mining activity, contamination, services, and the feasibility and cost of their proposed use. auction_events.description: Commercial Development Auction House Birmingham are proud to present this former brass foundry and ironmongers, offering investors and developers the opportunity to explore a new future for a distinctive piece of Wolverhampton’s industrial heritage. Historically associated with William Evans, Son & Co., the site’s manufacturing roots extend back to around 1854, with the present building believed to date from around 1870. The company’s activities included brass founding and lock manufacturing, followed by its longstanding role as an ironmongers and builders’ merchant. Council heritage records describe the property as a rare surviving example of a nineteenth-century industrial complex within the City, a compelling story for an investor seeking a project with its own identity. The property requires complete improvement and refurbishment throughout, presenting a substantial project for purchasers experienced in restoring and adapting older buildings. Its history could become a central feature of a sympathetic refurbishment, giving future accommodation a distinctive connection to Wolverhampton’s manufacturing past. Local authorities demolished the old Castlegate Shopping Centre to build the Stockton Waterfront . This major urban park space, three times the size of Trafalgar Square, features a seamless land bridge connecting the High Street directly back to the riverside for public community events. Prince Regent Street is a prominent, historically rich commercial street located in the heart of Stockton-on-Tees town centre. Serving as a key tertiary thoroughfare just a stone’s throw from Stockton High Street and connecting down toward Yarm Lane, it functions as a lively commercial parade characterized by a distinct mix of 19th- and 20th-century architecture.
